sentences.text: Probrachylophosaurus was a large, four-legged herbivore belonging to the subfamily Saurolophinae and the tribe Brachylophosaurini. This solid-crested hadrosaur possessed slender front limbs, strong hind limbs, and a long stiff tail. Its head featured a wide, backward-projecting crest supported by long striations along the frontal and nasal bones.
In this species, the frontals covering the nasal attachment area cover only about 59% of the frontal bone, compared to full coverage in adult Brachylophosaurus.
The holotype specimen of Probrachylophosaurus is the largest known member of the brachysaurolophine group. Due to its large size, this fossil was nicknamed "Super-Duck".
A specific specimen reached an age of fourteen years when it died, suggesting the holotype could be around that age as well.
The display crest on the head of Probrachylophosaurus grew significantly later in life than the rest of the skeleton.
The genus Probrachylophosaurus was described by Freedman Fowler and Horner in 2015.
The first fossils of Probrachylophosaurus were discovered in Montana in 1981, but the skeleton was not fully excavated until 2008.
The specific name 'bergei' honors Sam Berge, a landowner who supported the research.
Fossilized gut contents indicate that Probrachylophosaurus ate leaves, consistent with other hadrosaurs.
Studies indicate Probrachylophosaurus had a maximum growth rate of 855 kg per year between the ages of 3.64 and 4.64 years.

Histologic analysis indicates that Probrachylophosaurus experienced fast growth rates similar to other hadrosaurs. Sexual maturity in Probrachylophosaurus appears to have been reached at approximately five years of age.
A fourteen-year-old Probrachylophosaurus specimen had reached 95% of its maximum size by the age of nine.
The left tibia showed fourteen lines of arrested growth, which likely represent annual seasons of poor food consumption. Therefore, the age of the holotype could be around fourteen years old.

Evidence of injuries, including fractured tail vertebrae, suggests Probrachylophosaurus may have interacted aggressively with other hadrosaurs. The lower jaw of the type specimen shows three circular depressions surrounded by raised bone rings. Six vertebrae in the middle of the tail show healed breakage across their neural spines. Scientists have proposed multiple causes for tail injuries in hadrosaurs, including predator attacks, herd trampling, biomechanical stress, and mating behavior. Recent research suggests that mating behavior, specifically mounting by males, is the most likely cause of the healed tail injuries found in Probrachylophosaurus.
Probrachylophosaurus is thought to be a close relative of Brachylophosaurus and Ornatops and a possible descendant of Acristavus.

Fossils of Probrachylophosaurus date to the Campanian age between 80.45 and 79 million years ago. Probrachylophosaurus lived between 80.45 and 79.5 million years ago during the early Campanian stage of the Late Cretaceous.
The discovery of Probrachylophosaurus suggests that brachylophosaurs were among the first hadrosaurs to colonize fluvial lowlands after the Claggett Seaway receded.
It is debated whether the specimen Brachylophosaurus goodwini is a distinct species or merely a younger specimen of Probrachylophosaurus bergei.
Early phylogenetic analyses disagreed on whether Probrachylophosaurus was a close relative of Brachylophosaurus or a sister taxon to a group containing both Brachylophosaurus and Maiasaura.
